issue_results.scope_and_quantifiers: Theorem2.4 p7 concerns an upper rate-distortion dimension bound for every invariant probability measure. Theorem2.5 is existential for 0<=c<2(N+1)rho(CP^N), with equality of both dimensions for the constructed measure. It does not assert endpoint attainment or ergodicity. These distinctions and the periodic-orbit counterevidence are correctly retained.
bounded_independent_checks: The inverse estimate on p55 follows from ||w||_C<=2||w||_S<=2d+(1/4)||w||_C, hence ||w||_C<=8d/3. Normalized volume in complex dimension m scales with real exponent 2m. The small-diameter base is at most one, so substituting the dimension lower bound has the correct inequality direction.
The -2C_f L loss in p55 and the subsequent -C_f L on p56 differ only by an unspecified boundary constant, which vanishes after division by L^2. No leading coefficient is lost.

On p39 the cover needs its cardinality M, not log M. Defining M as the covering cardinality, tame growth gives tau^eta log_2 M<1, hence M^(tau^eta)<2. Counting exceptional subsets and their cover assignments contributes at most 4^(L^k), yielding the reported Frostman estimate with the stated exponent loss. This supports the notation-only classification.

On pp54-57, the strict derivative margin is preserved by dilation 0<lambda<1; changing variables gives rho(g(lambda dot))=lambda^2 rho(g). A point mass at a constant curve handles c=0. Averaging squares produces invariant limits because the normalized symmetric-difference area tends to zero. The supplied energy error is O(L), which vanishes after area normalization.
